title: Good centres in a minimum-length comparison of regular nodal models
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $T_1,T_2$ be integral regular schemes of dimension two [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], projective, flat and finitely presented over $S$ [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty nodal geometric curve fibres and smooth generic fibres. Fix a $K$-isomorphism $\alpha:(T_1)_K\cong(T_2)_K$. Suppose there exists a finite sequence $q_1:W=T_{1,m}\to\cdots\to T_{1,0}=T_1$ of blowups of reduced closed special-fibre points [def-nagata-global-blowup], together with an $S$-morphism $q_2:W\to T_2$ whose generic fibre is $\alpha\circ(q_1)_K$. Among all such pairs consisting of a sequence and a second morphism with this fixed generic identification, let this sequence have minimum length $m$. Then every centre $x_j\in (T_{1,j})_k$ lies in the relative smooth locus of $T_{1,j}\to S$ and its residue field $\kappa(x_j)$ is a finite separable extension of $k$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-separable-polynomial]. Here nodal geometric curve fibres means reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one whose nonsmooth closed points over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; the fibres may be disconnected.

proof.text: Write $X_i=T_{1,i}$, with $b_{i+1}:X_{i+1}\to X_i$ centred at $x_i$. The nodal local-chart statement gives Noetherianity, local dimension at most two and dimension two at closed special points of $T_1,T_2$. Flatness over the DVR makes the generic open dense: on every affine chart the uniformizer is a nonzerodivisor, hence misses the generic prime of this integral scheme. The point-blowup geometry and fibre-defect statements inductively give integral regular Noetherian projective flat surfaces $X_i$, unchanged on that dense generic open; their exceptional closed points have local dimension two and the same is true off each centre. Thus every centre has local dimension two and every stage is pure of dimension two. The terminal map $q_2$ is proper by projectivity of $W$ and separatedness of $T_2$, and birational because its generic restriction is the prescribed isomorphism. All centre fields are finite over $k$ by the closed-point field lemma applied to the finite-type special fibres.

source.place: Tags 0AGR (lemma-blowup-regular) and 0C5S (lemma-birational-regular-surfaces), proper birational second projection; local hypotheses from models.tex 0CDD.

proof.text: Every irreducible special-fibre component of $W$ which has coefficient $>1$ in $\operatorname{div}(\pi)$, or which is a strict transform of an exceptional $\mathbf P^1_l$ with $l/k$ inseparable, is contracted by $q_2$. Indeed, if such a component $D$ is not contracted, its image is a component $C$ of $(T_2)_k$. Apply the regular-trait component statement to $T_2$: projectivity gives properness, flatness and regularity are assumed, and step 1 gives Noetherianity and both local-dimension hypotheses. Its ordinary special fibre is reduced because its geometric special fibre is reduced by nodality. Thus the local ring at the generic point of $C$ is a DVR with maximal ideal $(\pi)$. The normal-modification statement then makes $q_2$ an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of this point. Hence the coefficient on $D$ is one, excluding the first case. In the second case $k(D)=l(t)$ by strict-transform persistence and the same isomorphism identifies it with $k(C)$. Apply the birational geometric-reduction statement with ground field $k$, geometrically reduced scheme $(T_2)_k$, component $C$, and both birational maps equal to $\mathrm{id}_C$. It says $k(C)\otimes_k L$ is reduced for every field extension $L/k$. This fails for $l(t)$: for an inseparable element of the finite extension $l/k$, its minimal polynomial has repeated roots over $\bar k$, giving a nonzero nilpotent in the corresponding simple subfield tensored with $\bar k$. Faithful scalar extension to $l(t)$ preserves this injection and this nilpotent. This contradiction excludes noncontraction. Properness makes the zero-dimensional irreducible image of a contracted $D$ a single closed point.

Suppose some centre is not smooth with separable residue field, and take the first one. Before it the models remain nodal by the good-centre clause of the fibre-defect statement (induction starting from $T_1$). If this centre is nonsmooth, its new exceptional component has coefficient two. Otherwise its residue extension is inseparable, and its new exceptional component is a $\mathbf P^1_l$ of the second bad type in step 2. Follow this component through the remaining blowups. Whenever a later centre lies on its current strict transform, replace the chosen component by that later blowup's exceptional component. The two persistence clauses ensure that the chosen component is still bad of the same type. The index of its birth strictly increases at each replacement, so the finite process terminates at an exceptional component $E$ which no later centre meets. Its final strict transform is contracted by step 2.

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), fibre-divisor defects and persistence under point blowups; agent finite last-descendant selection.

proof.text: Apply the untouched-blowup deletion statement to $X_m\to\cdots\to X_0$, this exceptional component, and $f=q_2$. It gives a sequence of length $m-1$ over $T_1$ and a descended $S$-map to $T_2$. Take $V=(T_1)_K$: every old centre is special, so the new centres are special too, and deletion preserves the generic identification $\alpha$. This is one of the pairs over which $m$ was minimized, a contradiction. Thus every centre is smooth with separable residue field; finiteness was proved in step 1. For $m=0$ the conclusion is vacuous.
